phases.name: Marathon Recovery
phases.tagline: Two weeks of genuine recovery after 26.2. Rebuild, don't rebuild fitness yet.
focus: Let the marathon damage fully heal — walking, easy movement, mobility.
Start easy swimming: zero-impact AND it opens the triathlon's first discipline.
Keep the knee quiet; reintroduce eccentric step-downs by week 2 if pain-free.

items.label: Rest / walk
items.detail: Full rest or an easy walk

phases.lifting: Minimal — mobility and light bodyweight only. No loading yet.

nutrition.mindset: Recovery fueling. Eat at maintenance, protein high to rebuild. No deficit — this is repair time.

phases.notes: First running should feel easy and short (~2–3 mi) only once legs feel normal — likely end of week 2.

phases.name: Triathlon Build + Power Base
phases.tagline: Reduced running frees recovery for the gym — build swim + bike, and start the dunk base concurrently.
focus: Swim + bike are the build; run drops to 2–3×/wk (already locked) — which protects the knee.
Grow the long bike toward 56 mi; hold swim to a comfortable 2,000 m.
Strength is PRIMARY here — build the power base for the dunk while endurance running is low.
Introduce calisthenics: handstand daily, lever/planche progressions in the gym.

items.label: Quality run
items.detail: Tempo / threshold — the one hard run

phases.lifting: PRIMARY — build. 2–3×/wk progressive: max strength + power (this IS the dunk base). Add straight-arm calisthenics.

nutrition.mindset: Fuel to perform, slow recomp at maintenance. Don't hard-cut — the build comes first. Abs emerge slowly from reduced running + lifting.
macros: Carbs cycled: higher on long-bike/run days, moderate otherwise

phases.notes: Bricks (bike→run) in the last ~6 weeks. Power work always before endurance on doubled days. Knee vetoes plyos before it vetoes runs.

phases.name: Block 1 — Power, Speed & Lean
phases.priority: Dunk by Dec 31 · rebuild upper body · get lean · mile/5K speed
phases.tagline: Post-Napa off-season: endurance volume drops, freeing recovery for power + muscle. Four threads that reinforce each other — dunk (lower power), mile/5K speed, upper-body rebuild, and a lean recomp. Running alone covers the cardio base (no bike/swim this block).
focus: Dunk: max strength → reactive plyo → jump technique, peaked in December on fresh legs.
Upper-body rebuild: 2 push + 2 pull/week — the off-season is the ideal window (and it comes back fast).
Mile/5K speed: one quality run/week (reps, hills, fartlek) — which also maintains the aerobic base.
Lean recomp: gentle ~0.5 lb/wk cut, high protein — better power-to-weight AND visible abs.

items.label: Speed run
items.detail: Mile/5K reps — the one hard run

phases.lifting: PRIMARY — power + hypertrophy. Lower strength + plyo (fresh) 2×; upper push + pull 2× (the rebuild). Peak phase shifts to heavy-but-brief + reactive plyo.

nutrition.mindset: Gentle cut (~0.5 lb/wk) — the only real cut window. High protein holds muscle & power; regaining upper body in a slight deficit works. The India/Vietnam trip (Nov 15–Dec 6) is a planned diet break — eat at maintenance.
macros: Carbs cycled: fuel lifting/speed days, deficit on easy/rest days
Deficit ~300–500 kcal; diet break on the trip

phases.notes: Trip Nov 15–Dec 6 = equipment-light (bodyweight power + upper + running). Jumps/plyo always FRESH, never after heavy lifts or hard runs. Knee staples (step-downs) stay in daily — plyo gets vetoed before anything else. Full day-by-day plan at /dunk.

phases.name: Block 2 — Marathon PR Build
phases.priority: A big marathon PR at a spring race — sub-3:40, stretch sub-3:30
phases.tagline: Take the speed built in Block 1 and extend it to 26.2. Upper body drops to maintenance, mileage ramps. The 3:53 was a knee-comeback race off minimal training — with a real build and that 5:36 mile, a big PR is on the table. This marathon fitness also becomes the launchpad for the Ironman run.
focus: Rebuild running volume + long run from the Block 1 base.
Marathon-pace + threshold work; carry the mile/5K top-end speed into endurance.
Pick a late-April/May 2027 marathon — clean recovery before the IM build.
Strength drops to 2× maintenance; keep the knee staples.
phases.lifting: Maintenance — 1–2×/wk, heavy-but-brief. Injury prevention + preserve power. Never zero.

nutrition.mindset: Fuel the mileage — eat at maintenance, carb-cycle around long runs & quality. No cutting; performance first.
macros: No deficit during the marathon build

phases.notes: The marathon can be a peak-and-taper race OR a hard tune-up within the bigger endurance year — your call closer to the date.

phases.name: Block 3 — Ironman California Build
phases.tagline: Long-course endurance — bike-heavy (knee-friendly). The spring marathon fitness carries the IM run. Apply the two Napa lessons: pace the bike by HR (not ego) and take ≥500 mg sodium/hr.
focus: Rebuild swim + bike (both detrain slowly / return fast); long bike is the anchor.
Brick work; dial in pacing by HR and a sodium-adequate fuel plan.
Run volume stays moderate off the marathon base — protects the knee.
IRONMAN California late Oct 2027 (Texas Apr 2027 sold out).
phases.lifting: Maintenance — 1–2×/wk. Preserve muscle & power against the volume; it's catabolic otherwise.

nutrition.mindset: Fuel to perform — maintain leanness, NEVER under-fuel. Getting leaner here = RED-S risk (health, not just physique). High energy flux keeps you lean AND fueled.
macros: Eat at high maintenance; accept softer abs at rest = fuel, not fat

phases.notes: IM entry ~$700–900, peak 12–18 hrs/wk. Sub-5 mile is parked to 2028 — it can't coexist with this volume.

phases.name: Speed Year & Beyond
phases.priority: Sub-5:00 mile + start the BQ ladder
phases.tagline: Low-fatigue speed focus for the mile, then begin laddering the marathon toward the 2:55 north star.
focus: Dedicated track/speed block for the sub-5:00 mile — needs fresh legs, low volume.
Then begin the marathon ladder: 3:29 → 3:15 → 3:05, only as the knee proves it holds mileage.
Maintain the dunk, tri fitness, and calisthenics as background threads.
Calisthenics can push again here (lower endurance fatigue).

nutrition.mindset: Fuel to perform; lean maintenance. Speed work rewards being light but well-fueled.

phases.notes: Sub-5 mile VDOT roughly predicts a ~2:55–3:00 marathon with endurance — it's the speed key to the BQ.

roadmap.title: Constant Threads
items: Durability: knee staples + prehab, every phase
Race lessons: pace the bike by HR, sodium ≥500 mg/hr
Nutrition: fuel to perform, cut only in the dunk block

durability: Prehab strength 2×/wk, always — posterior chain, single-leg, glute med/hips, calves, core.
Knee staples forever: eccentric step-downs, quad/VMO, glute strength (PFPS insurance).
Load management: gradual progression, stepback weeks every 3–4 wks, no big jumps (remember the 37-mi tandem).
Early-warning discipline: back off at 'awareness', don't wait for pain.
Wrist/shoulder prep before planche & lever work — tendons adapt slower than muscle.
Cross-training bias (swim/bike) spreads load off the joints — structural knee protection.
Sleep + recovery are training. One full rest day, always.
nutrition_principles: Protein is the constant: ~0.8–1 g/lb (~150–170g) in every phase.
Carbs are the lever: high to fuel endurance/power builds, moderate & timed during the cut.
Cut ONLY in the dunk block (late 2026). Everywhere else: fuel to perform or maintain.
The endurance-athlete danger is UNDER-fueling (RED-S), not overeating. Fuel enough.
High energy flux (eat a lot, burn a lot) keeps you lean AND recovered — that's the goal.
Get lean before the Ironman year, then maintain by eating-to-fuel — never cut mid-build.
Leanness serves the dunk AND calisthenics (strength-to-weight). One lever, several goals.

muscle_maintenance.intro: During endurance-heavy phases (tri/IM builds), the goal shifts from building to NOT LOSING muscle. Research is clear: you keep strength on remarkably little — as little as 1 hard set per muscle 2×/week maintains it, IF the load stays heavy. So maintenance is about intensity (keep lifting heavy), not volume. Hit every movement pattern below 2×/week and you won't lose a thing.
rules: Keep the load HEAVY (~80–85%, 4–6 reps). Light-and-fluffy is what loses muscle — heavy-but-brief preserves it.
2×/week per muscle is enough to maintain. You don't need more during a build.
Cover all 6 patterns: squat, hinge, horizontal push, vertical push, horizontal pull, vertical pull — plus single-leg + core.
Leave 1–2 reps in reserve. Maintenance ≠ grinding to failure; that just adds fatigue that steals from your endurance sessions.
Protein ~0.8–1 g/lb is half the battle — you can't hold muscle underfed.
It's fine to superset opposing movements (push/pull) to save time on a busy build.
